1603	// Constants for formatting output
1604	const (
1605		// maxIntentDisplayLength is the maximum length for intent text before truncation
1606		maxIntentDisplayLength = 80
1607		// maxMessageDisplayLength is the maximum length for checkpoint messages before truncation
1608		maxMessageDisplayLength = 80
1609		// maxPromptDisplayLength is the maximum length for session prompts before truncation
1610		maxPromptDisplayLength = 60
1611		// checkpointIDDisplayLength is the number of characters to show from checkpoint IDs
1612		checkpointIDDisplayLength = 12
1613	)
1614	
1615	// formatBranchCheckpoints formats checkpoint information for a branch.
1616	// Groups commits by checkpoint ID and shows the prompt for each checkpoint.
1617	// If sessionFilter is non-empty, only shows checkpoints matching that session ID (or prefix).
1618	func formatBranchCheckpoints(branchName string, points []strategy.RewindPoint, sessionFilter string) string {
1619		var sb strings.Builder
1620	
1621		// Branch header
1622		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Branch: %s\n", branchName)
1623	
1624		// Filter by session if specified
1625		if sessionFilter != "" {
1626			var filtered []strategy.RewindPoint
1627			for _, p := range points {
1628				if p.SessionID == sessionFilter || strings.HasPrefix(p.SessionID, sessionFilter) {
1629					filtered = append(filtered, p)
1630				}
1631			}
1632			points = filtered
1633		}
1634	
1635		if len(points) == 0 {
1636			sb.WriteString("Checkpoints: 0\n")
1637			if sessionFilter != "" {
1638				fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Filtered by session: %s\n", sessionFilter)
1639			}
1640			sb.WriteString("\nNo checkpoints found on this branch.\n")
1641			sb.WriteString("Checkpoints will appear here after you save changes during a Claude session.\n")
1642			return sb.String()
1643		}
1644	
1645		// Group by checkpoint ID
1646		groups := groupByCheckpointID(points)
1647	
1648		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Checkpoints: %d\n", len(groups))
1649		if sessionFilter != "" {
1650			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Filtered by session: %s\n", sessionFilter)
1651		}
1652		sb.WriteString("\n")
1653	
1654		// Output each checkpoint group
1655		for _, group := range groups {
1656			formatCheckpointGroup(&sb, group)
1657			sb.WriteString("\n")
1658		}
1659	
1660		return sb.String()
1661	}
1662	
1663	// checkpointGroup represents a group of commits sharing the same checkpoint ID.
1664	type checkpointGroup struct {
1665		checkpointID string
1666		prompt       string
1667		isTemporary  bool // true if any commit is not logs-only (can be rewound)
1668		isTask       bool // true if this is a task checkpoint
1669		commits      []commitEntry
1670	}
1671	
1672	// commitEntry represents a single git commit within a checkpoint.
1673	type commitEntry struct {
1674		date    time.Time
1675		gitSHA  string // short git SHA
1676		message string
1677	}
1678	
1679	// groupByCheckpointID groups rewind points by their checkpoint ID.
1680	// Returns groups sorted by latest commit timestamp (most recent first).
1681	func groupByCheckpointID(points []strategy.RewindPoint) []checkpointGroup {
1682		if len(points) == 0 {
1683			return nil
1684		}
1685	
1686		// Build map of checkpoint ID -> group
1687		groupMap := make(map[string]*checkpointGroup)
1688		var order []string // Track insertion order for stable iteration
1689	
1690		for _, point := range points {
1691			// Determine the checkpoint ID to use for grouping
1692			cpID := point.CheckpointID.String()
1693			if cpID == "" {
1694				// Temporary checkpoints: group by session ID to preserve per-session prompts
1695				// Use session ID prefix for readability (format: YYYY-MM-DD-uuid)
1696				cpID = point.SessionID
1697				if cpID == "" {
1698					cpID = "temporary" // Fallback if no session ID
1699				}
1700			}
1701	
1702			group, exists := groupMap[cpID]
1703			if !exists {
1704				group = &checkpointGroup{
1705					checkpointID: cpID,
1706					prompt:       point.SessionPrompt,
1707					isTemporary:  !point.IsLogsOnly,
1708					isTask:       point.IsTaskCheckpoint,
1709				}
1710				groupMap[cpID] = group
1711				order = append(order, cpID)
1712			}
1713	
1714			// Short git SHA (7 chars)
1715			gitSHA := point.ID
1716			if len(gitSHA) > 7 {
1717				gitSHA = gitSHA[:7]
1718			}
1719	
1720			group.commits = append(group.commits, commitEntry{
1721				date:    point.Date,
1722				gitSHA:  gitSHA,
1723				message: point.Message,
1724			})
1725	
1726			// Update flags - if any commit is temporary/task, the group is too
1727			if !point.IsLogsOnly {
1728				group.isTemporary = true
1729			}
1730			if point.IsTaskCheckpoint {
1731				group.isTask = true
1732			}
1733			// Update prompt if the group's prompt is empty but this point has one
1734			if group.prompt == "" && point.SessionPrompt != "" {
1735				group.prompt = point.SessionPrompt
1736			}
1737		}
1738	
1739		// Sort commits within each group by date (most recent first)
1740		for _, group := range groupMap {
1741			sort.Slice(group.commits, func(i, j int) bool {
1742				return group.commits[i].date.After(group.commits[j].date)
1743			})
1744		}
1745	
1746		// Build result slice in order, then sort by latest commit
1747		result := make([]checkpointGroup, 0, len(order))
1748		for _, cpID := range order {
1749			result = append(result, *groupMap[cpID])
1750		}
1751	
1752		// Sort groups by latest commit timestamp (most recent first)
1753		sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
1754			// Each group's commits are already sorted, so first commit is latest
1755			if len(result[i].commits) == 0 {
1756				return false
1757			}
1758			if len(result[j].commits) == 0 {
1759				return true
1760			}
1761			return result[i].commits[0].date.After(result[j].commits[0].date)
1762		})
1763	
1764		return result
1765	}
1766	
1767	// formatCheckpointGroup formats a single checkpoint group for display.
1768	func formatCheckpointGroup(sb *strings.Builder, group checkpointGroup) {
1769		// Checkpoint ID (truncated for display)
1770		cpID := group.checkpointID
1771		if len(cpID) > checkpointIDDisplayLength {
1772			cpID = cpID[:checkpointIDDisplayLength]
1773		}
1774	
1775		// Build status indicators
1776		// Skip [temporary] indicator when cpID is already "temporary" to avoid redundancy
1777		var indicators []string
1778		if group.isTask {
1779			indicators = append(indicators, "[Task]")
1780		}
1781		if group.isTemporary && cpID != "temporary" {
1782			indicators = append(indicators, "[temporary]")
1783		}
1784	
1785		indicatorStr := ""
1786		if len(indicators) > 0 {
1787			indicatorStr = " " + strings.Join(indicators, " ")
1788		}
1789	
1790		// Prompt (truncated)
1791		var promptStr string
1792		if group.prompt == "" {
1793			promptStr = "(no prompt)"
1794		} else {
1795			// Quote actual prompts
1796			promptStr = fmt.Sprintf("%q", strategy.TruncateDescription(group.prompt, maxPromptDisplayLength))
1797		}
1798	
1799		// Checkpoint header: [checkpoint_id] [indicators] prompt
1800		fmt.Fprintf(sb, "[%s]%s %s\n", cpID, indicatorStr, promptStr)
1801	
1802		// List commits under this checkpoint
1803		for _, commit := range group.commits {
1804			// Format: "  MM-DD HH:MM (git_sha) message"
1805			dateTimeStr := commit.date.Format("01-02 15:04")
1806			message := strategy.TruncateDescription(commit.message, maxMessageDisplayLength)
1807			fmt.Fprintf(sb, "  %s (%s) %s\n", dateTimeStr, commit.gitSHA, message)
1808		}
1809	}
1810	
1811	// countLines counts the number of lines in a byte slice.
1812	// For JSONL content (where each line ends with \n), this returns the line count.
1813	// Empty content returns 0.
1814	func countLines(content []byte) int {
1815		if len(content) == 0 {
1816			return 0
1817		}
1818		count := 0
1819		for _, b := range content {
1820			if b == '\n' {
1821				count++
1822			}
1823		}
1824		return count
1825	}
1826	
1827	// transcriptOffset returns the appropriate offset for scoping a transcript.
1828	// For Claude Code (JSONL), this is the line count. For Gemini (JSON), this is the message count.
1829	func transcriptOffset(transcriptBytes []byte, agentType types.AgentType) int {
1830		switch agentType {
1831		case agent.AgentTypeGemini:
1832			t, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript(transcriptBytes)
1833			if err != nil {
1834				return 0
1835			}
1836			return len(t.Messages)
1837		case agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, agent.AgentTypeOpenCode, agent.AgentTypeCursor, agent.AgentTypeFactoryAIDroid, agent.AgentTypeUnknown:
1838			return countLines(transcriptBytes)
1839		}
1840		return countLines(transcriptBytes)
1841	}
1842	
1843	// hasCodeChanges returns true if the commit has changes to non-metadata files.
1844	// Uses a full tree diff to distinguish code changes from .entire/ metadata-only changes.
1845	// Returns false only if the commit has a parent AND only modified .entire/ metadata files.
1846	//
1847	// WARNING: This is expensive via go-git (resolves many tree/blob objects from packfiles).
1848	// For list views with many checkpoints, use hasAnyChanges instead.
1849	func hasCodeChanges(commit *object.Commit) bool {
1850		// First commit on shadow branch captures working copy state - always meaningful
1851		if commit.NumParents() == 0 {
1852			return true
1853		}
1854	
1855		parent, err := commit.Parent(0)
1856		if err != nil {
1857			return true // Can't check, assume meaningful
1858		}
1859	
1860		commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
1861		if err != nil {
1862			return true
1863		}
1864	
1865		parentTree, err := parent.Tree()
1866		if err != nil {
1867			return true
1868		}
1869	
1870		changes, err := parentTree.Diff(commitTree)
1871		if err != nil {
1872			return true
1873		}
1874	
1875		// Check if any non-metadata file was changed
1876		for _, change := range changes {
1877			name := change.To.Name
1878			if name == "" {
1879				name = change.From.Name
1880			}
1881			// Skip .entire/ metadata files
1882			if !strings.HasPrefix(name, ".entire/") {
1883				return true
1884			}
1885		}
1886	
1887		return false
1888	}
1889	
1890	// hasAnyChanges is a lightweight alternative to hasCodeChanges that compares
1891	// tree hashes without doing a full diff. Returns true if the commit's tree
1892	// differs from its parent's tree. This may include metadata-only changes,
1893	// but is O(1) instead of O(files) — suitable for list views.
1894	func hasAnyChanges(commit *object.Commit) bool {
1895		if commit.NumParents() == 0 {
1896			return true
1897		}
1898		parent, err := commit.Parent(0)
1899		if err != nil {
1900			return true
1901		}
1902		return commit.TreeHash != parent.TreeHash
1903	}

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"## Summary
Adds a timeout to checkpoint summary generation for `entire explain --generate` so the command cannot hang indefinitely when the Claude CLI stalls.

## What Changed
- scopes the 30 second timeout to `explain --generate` in `explain.go`
- keeps `summarize.GenerateFromTranscript` generic for other call sites
- preserves shorter parent deadlines and clamps longer parent deadlines to the 30 second safety timeout
- improves Claude CLI cancellation and deadline handling so context cancellation surfaces cleanly
- prints `Generating checkpoint summary...` while `explain --generate` is waiting
- adds unit coverage for default timeout, shorter parent deadline, longer parent deadline, and cancellation behavior

## Why
A stalled Claude summary generation path currently leaves users waiting without a bounded failure mode. This change keeps the fix narrowly scoped to `explain --generate` instead of changing shared summarize behavior for other callers.

1	// Package agent provides interfaces and types for integrating with coding agents.
2	// It abstracts agent-specific behavior (hooks, log parsing, session storage) so that
3	// the same Strategy implementations can work with any coding agent.
4	package agent
5	
6	import (
7		"context"

11	)

13	// Agent defines the interface for interacting with a coding agent.
14	// Each agent implementation (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, etc.) converts its
15	// native format to the normalized types defined in this package.
16	//
17	// The interface is organized into three groups:
18	//   - Identity (5 methods): Name, Type, Description, DetectPresence, ProtectedDirs
19	//   - Transcript Storage (3 methods): ReadTranscript, ChunkTranscript, ReassembleTranscript
20	//   - Legacy (6 methods): Will be moved to optional interfaces or removed in a future phase
21	type Agent interface {
22		// --- Identity ---
23	
24		// Name returns the agent registry key (e.g., "claude-code", "gemini")
25		Name() types.AgentName
26	
27		// Type returns the agent type identifier (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI")
28		// This is stored in metadata and trailers.
29		Type() types.AgentType
30	
31		// Description returns a human-readable description for UI
32		Description() string
33	
34		// IsPreview returns whether the agent integration is in preview or stable
35		IsPreview() bool
36	
37		// DetectPresence checks if this agent is configured in the repository
38		DetectPresence(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)
39	
40		// ProtectedDirs returns repo-root-relative directories that should never be
41		// modified or deleted during rewind or other destructive operations.
42		// Examples: [".claude"] for Claude, [".gemini"] for Gemini.
43		ProtectedDirs() []string

45		// --- Transcript Storage ---

47		// ReadTranscript reads the raw transcript bytes for a session.

49	
50		// ChunkTranscript splits a transcript into chunks if it exceeds maxSize.
51		// Returns a slice of chunks. If the transcript fits in one chunk, returns single-element slice.
52		// The chunking is format-aware: JSONL splits at line boundaries, JSON splits message arrays.
53		ChunkTranscript(ctx context.Context, content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error)
54	
55		// ReassembleTranscript combines chunks back into a single transcript.
56		// Handles format-specific reassembly (JSONL concatenation, JSON message merging).
57		ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error)

76		// FormatResumeCommand returns command to resume a session.
77		FormatResumeCommand(sessionID string) string
78	}

80	// HookSupport is implemented by agents with lifecycle hooks.
81	// This optional interface allows agents like Claude Code and Cursor to
82	// install and manage hooks that notify Entire of agent events.

84	// The interface is organized into two groups:
85	//   - Hook Mapping (2 methods): HookNames, ParseHookEvent
86	//   - Hook Management (3 methods): InstallHooks, UninstallHooks, AreHooksInstalled

88		Agent

92		// e.g., ["stop", "user-prompt-submit", "session-start", "session-end"]
93		HookNames() []string

95		// ParseHookEvent translates an agent-native hook into a normalized lifecycle Event.
96		// Returns nil if the hook has no lifecycle significance (e.g., pass-through hooks).
97		// This is the core contribution surface for new agent implementations.
98		ParseHookEvent(ctx context.Context, hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*Event, error)
99	
100		// InstallHooks installs agent-specific hooks.
101		// If localDev is true, hooks point to local development build.
102		// If force is true, removes existing Entire hooks before installing.
103		// Returns the number of hooks installed.
104		InstallHooks(ctx context.Context, localDev bool, force bool) (int, error)
105	
106		// UninstallHooks removes installed hooks
107		UninstallHooks(ctx context.Context) error
108	
109		// AreHooksInstalled checks if hooks are currently installed

111	}
112

114	// Agents like Aider that don't support hooks can use file watching

117		Agent

119		// GetWatchPaths returns paths to watch for session changes

121

129	// via git-status-based file detection and raw transcript storage.

138

144		//   - currentPosition: the current position (line count or message count)

147	}

151	// Droid's exec mode doesn't fire UserPromptSubmit).

153		Agent

156		ExtractPrompts(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) ([]string, error)
157	}

160	// flush/sync requirements (e.g., Claude Code's async transcript writing).

163		Agent

168	}

177	}

content.text:
I have enough now to give you a real evaluation. Here's what I found and what I'd change.

## What the current code actually does

Three layers, with PR 876's timeout at the top:

1. **`cli/explain.go::generateCheckpointAISummary`** wraps the call in a 30s context (`checkpointSummaryTimeout`), translates `DeadlineExceeded`/`Canceled` into "summary generation timed out after 30s" / "canceled"
2. **`summarize/claude.go::ClaudeGenerator.Generate`** is agent-agnostic — it calls `agent.TextGenerator.GenerateText(...)` and then JSON-parses the result
3. **`agent/claudecode/generate.go::ClaudeCodeAgent.GenerateText`** is where `claude --print --output-format json --model X --setting-sources ""` actually runs and where stdout/stderr/exit codes are observed

## Two important findings that change the plan

**Finding 1: Codex's plan puts the typed error and stdout-parsing in the wrong file.** `summarize/claude.go` doesn't run a subprocess and doesn't see stderr/exit codes — it goes through `agent.TextGenerator`. Adding `ClaudeDebugOptions`/`buildClaudeCommand`/`--debug api --debug-file` flags there is architecturally wrong. The natural seam for typed-error extraction and any debug-flag wiring is `agent/claudecode/generate.go` + `agent/claudecode/response.go`. The `summarize` layer is supposed to stay agent-agnostic so that Gemini/OpenCode/etc. can also generate summaries someday — putting Claude-specific debug-file plumbing in `summarize/` poisons that abstraction.

**Finding 2: Codex's "parse stdout on non-zero exit" condition is wrong.** I just probed the live Claude CLI:

| Failure | Exit code | Stdout |
|---|---|---|
| invalid model (`--model nonexistent`) | **0** | `{"is_error":true,"api_error_status":404,"result":"There's an issue with the selected model..."}` |
| empty model | **0** | `{"is_error":true,"api_error_status":400,"result":"API Error: 400 ... invalid_request_error ..."}` |
| binary missing | 127 | (shell error) |

So the most useful errors return **exit 0** with `is_error: true`, and the current `parseGenerateTextResponse` discards both `is_error` and `subtype`. That means today, an invalid model gets re-parsed as Summary JSON and the user sees something like `failed to parse summary JSON: ... (response: There's an issue with the selected model...)`. Gating typed-error extraction on "non-zero exit" misses every case I just reproduced.

## My take on each step of the plan

1. **Clean up earlier ad-hoc edits** — agree.
2. **Parse Claude envelope (`is_error`, `subtype`, `result`, `duration_ms`)** — agree, but do it in `agent/claudecode/response.go`, and run the check **regardless of exit code**, not only on non-zero exit.
3. **Typed error model with kinds (auth/config/rate_limit/connection/cli_missing/timeout/unknown)** — agree on the kinds. Define the type in `agent/claudecode` (or a small shared `agentlerr` package if you don't want claude types leaking up). Have `summarize/claude.go` propagate it untouched via `%w` so explain.go can `errors.As` it. Map `is_error: true` + `api_error_status` ranges (401/403→auth, 429→rate_limit, 4xx→config, 5xx/network→connection) plus stderr substring matches for a few well-known auth/login phrases.
4. **Temp `--debug-file` for connection-classification** — **drop this for now.** It adds: a temp file lifecycle, a privacy-sensitive log read (debug logs may contain prompt content — your CLAUDE.md is explicit about not logging user content), brittle pattern matching against an internal Claude CLI debug format that can change between releases, and an extra subprocess flag that you'll need to keep working forever. All for *one* error category. If users actually report ambiguous timeouts in practice, add this later. Apply YAGNI here.
5. **Timeout-log classifier** — drop along with #4.
6. **Keep 30s as anti-hang stop** — partially agree. Two concerns:
   - **30s is genuinely tight for `sonnet` on a long checkpoint transcript.** The default model is `sonnet` (`summarize/claude.go:51`). My quick haiku probe took 2.7s on a 9-token prompt; a real summarization with a multi-KB transcript on sonnet will routinely brush 20–30s even when nothing's wrong. I'd bump the default to **60s** and make it overridable via `settings.local.json` (e.g., `summary_timeout_seconds: 60`). The "anti-hang" job is still done; users with slow connections aren't punished by a too-tight ceiling.
   - Drop the "if connection-classified" branch in the timeout error since we're dropping the debug-log classifier.
7. **Delayed "Still waiting…" message** — agree, this is cheap and helpful. ~10s feels right.
8. **Map typed errors to user-facing messages in explain.go** — agree. Keep the strings here (`formatCheckpointSummaryError` is the right helper name).
9. **Tests** — agree, but skip the debug-log classifier tests.
10. **Verify in layers** — fine.

## Things the plan misses that I'd add

- **Fix the double-wrap in error output.** Your PR description shows `failed to generate summary: failed to generate summary: claude CLI failed (exit -1):` — that's `explain.go` wrapping `summarize.GenerateFromTranscript` wrapping `agent/claudecode/generate.go`. After typed errors land, drop one of the two `failed to generate summary:` wrappers (probably the inner one in `GenerateFromTranscript`) so the final user-facing message is clean.
- **Honor `is_error` on exit 0.** This is the single highest-value change. Without it, an invalid model or 4xx API error today gets misreported as a JSON parse failure on the summary output.
- **Differentiate subtypes.** `subtype: "error_max_turns"` and `subtype: "error_during_execution"` have meaningful, different user advice. If you're already parsing the envelope, branch on subtype too.

## Recommended slimmed-down plan

Roughly half the surface area, ~all the value:

1. In `agent/claudecode/response.go`: extend the envelope to `{Type, Subtype, IsError, APIErrorStatus, Result}`. Add `ClaudeCLIError` type with `Kind` (auth / config / rate_limit / cli_missing / unknown) + `Message` + `APIStatus`.
2. In `agent/claudecode/generate.go`: after `cmd.Run()` succeeds OR fails, always try `parseGenerateTextResponse`. If `is_error: true`, classify by `api_error_status` + a small stderr substring table, return `ClaudeCLIError`. Keep the `exec.Error` → cli_missing path. Keep ctx.Err() handling.
3. In `cli/explain.go`: add `formatCheckpointSummaryError` that uses `errors.As` to map `ClaudeCLIError.Kind` and `context.DeadlineExceeded`/`Canceled` to user-facing strings. Add the delayed "Still waiting…" goroutine.
4. Bump `defaultCheckpointSummaryTimeout` to 60s, make it settings-overridable.
5. Tests: claude_test.go covers envelope parsing for `is_error: true` + each `api_error_status` band; explain_test.go covers the user-facing message for each kind + the delayed-message cancel behavior.
6. Drop the debug-file path entirely.

Net result: fast real failures get accurate, actionable messages; slow-but-real cases get a wider window before hitting a still-bounded fallback; the Claude-specific stuff stays in the Claude package; the `summarize` abstraction stays clean.

Want me to write this up as a proper design doc (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-15-explain-summary-error-classification-design.md`) and walk it through the brainstorming spec-review loop, or do you want to push back/refine any of the above first?

Good catch — the answer is nuanced and worth pinning down before I write the doc.

## Which exit code each kind comes from

Based on my live probes against the actual `claude` CLI:

| Kind | Trigger | Exit code | Where observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **auth** | `is_error: true` + `api_error_status: 401/403` (or stderr matches "Invalid API key" / "not logged in") | **0** | stdout JSON envelope |
| **rate_limit** | `is_error: true` + `api_error_status: 429` | **0** | stdout JSON envelope |
| **config** | `is_error: true` + `api_error_status: 4xx` (other than 401/403/429) — invalid model, malformed args | **0** | stdout JSON envelope (I confirmed: 400 + 404) |
| **cli_missing** | `exec.Error` (binary not on PATH) | n/a — process never starts | `errors.As(&exec.Error)` |
| **timeout** | `ctx.Err() == DeadlineExceeded` | -1 (signal-killed) | context, not exit code |
| **unknown** | non-zero exit with no parseable envelope, or any unmapped envelope | non-zero | stderr fallback |
| ~~connection~~ | (was going to come from debug-log classifier) | — | **dropped** |

So to answer directly: **the auth/config/rate_limit kinds happen on exit 0**, before the timeout, because the Claude CLI completes the subprocess "successfully" and reports the error inside its JSON envelope. Codex's "parse on non-zero exit" gate would miss every one of these. The classifier needs to run on **every** exit-0 result too, checking `is_error` first.

A few honest gaps worth calling out in the doc:

- **`connection` is dropped from the kinds list.** Without the debug-file (which we're deleting per #4–#5), we can't reliably tell "Claude tried Anthropic and got `ECONNREFUSED`" from "Claude is just slow." If `api_error_status` ever returns 5xx for network errors, we *could* map 5xx→connection — but I haven't verified that the CLI does this for network failures (vs. surfacing them as a hang or a non-zero exit with stderr). Safer to keep the kind list smaller and accept that connection issues fall into `timeout` or `unknown` for now.
- **stderr substring matching for auth** is a fallback for the case where Claude exits non-zero (e.g., a CLI version that crashes during auth check before producing the envelope). Cheap to add, brittle by nature — keep the list of phrases small (1–2 known strings) and treat it as "best effort, will improve as we see real reports."

# Design: Actionable error classification for `entire explain --generate`

**Date:** 2026-04-15
**Status:** Draft, awaiting review
**Related PR:** #876 (added the 30s timeout this design is refining)

## Problem

PR #876 added a 30-second timeout around checkpoint summary generation so that
`entire explain --generate` can no longer hang indefinitely when the Claude CLI
stalls. That fix replaced a "hangs forever, user has to Ctrl+C" failure with a
"hangs for 30 seconds, then prints `summary generation timed out after 30s`"
failure.

Two follow-up problems remain:

1. **Real Claude CLI failures are misclassified as parse failures or as
   ambiguous timeouts.** The Claude CLI returns most operational failures
   (auth, rate limit, invalid model, malformed request) as **exit 0** with a
   structured `is_error: true` envelope on stdout. The current code discards
   `is_error` and tries to JSON-parse the error string as a `Summary`, so the
   user sees `failed to parse summary JSON: ... (response: <error text>)`. That
   message is unactionable.
2. **The 30s timeout message is generic.** When it fires, the user has no way
   to tell whether Claude was actually hung, was slow on a long transcript, or
   had a network problem.

A third, smaller issue worth fixing in the same change:

3. **Errors get double-wrapped.** Today's output reads
   `failed to generate summary: failed to generate summary: claude CLI failed (exit -1):`
   because both `summarize.GenerateFromTranscript` and
   `cli/explain.go::generateCheckpointSummary` wrap with the same prefix.

## Current code path

Three layers, top to bottom:

1. `cli/explain.go::generateCheckpointAISummary` — wraps the call in a 30s
   `context.WithTimeout`, translates `DeadlineExceeded` and `Canceled` into
   user-facing strings.
2. `summarize/claude.go::ClaudeGenerator.Generate` — agent-agnostic; calls
   `agent.TextGenerator.GenerateText(...)` and JSON-parses the result string
   into a `checkpoint.Summary`.
3. `agent/claudecode/generate.go::ClaudeCodeAgent.GenerateText` — runs
   `claude --print --output-format json --model X --setting-sources ""`,
   observes stdout/stderr/exit codes, dispatches the response through
   `agent/claudecode/response.go::parseGenerateTextResponse`.

The seam where stdout, stderr, and exit code are all visible is layer 3 —
`agent/claudecode`. Anything that needs to read the Claude error envelope or
classify by `api_error_status` belongs there.

## Findings from probing the live `claude` CLI

These results drive the design:

| Failure                                  | Exit | stdout JSON                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Success                                  | 0    | `{"is_error":false, "subtype":"success", "result":"..."}`           |
| Invalid model (`--model nonexistent`)    | 0    | `{"is_error":true, "api_error_status":404, "result":"There's an issue with the selected model..."}` |
| Empty model (`--model ""`)               | 0    | `{"is_error":true, "api_error_status":400, "result":"API Error: 400 ... invalid_request_error ..."}` |
| Binary missing                           | 127  | (no envelope; produces `exec.Error` in Go)                          |

The two most useful insights:

- **Operational errors return exit 0**, not non-zero. Any classification gated
  on "non-zero exit" misses every probed failure mode. The envelope must be
  parsed and `is_error` checked **on every successful subprocess run**.
- **`subtype` and `api_error_status` are usable** for classification today.

## Design

### Layer 3 — `agent/claudecode/`

**Extend the response envelope** in `response.go`:

```go
type responseEnvelope struct {
    Type           string  `json:"type"`
    Subtype        string  `json:"subtype"`
    IsError        bool    `json:"is_error"`
    APIErrorStatus *int    `json:"api_error_status"`
    Result         *string `json:"result"`
}
```

`parseGenerateTextResponse` keeps its current "single object or array of
events" behavior, but also returns the parsed envelope (not just the result
string), so callers can branch on `IsError`.

**Add a typed error** in a new file `agent/claudecode/error.go`:

```go
type ClaudeErrorKind string

const (
    ClaudeErrorAuth       ClaudeErrorKind = "auth"
    ClaudeErrorConfig     ClaudeErrorKind = "config"
    ClaudeErrorRateLimit  ClaudeErrorKind = "rate_limit"
    ClaudeErrorCLIMissing ClaudeErrorKind = "cli_missing"
    ClaudeErrorUnknown    ClaudeErrorKind = "unknown"
)

type ClaudeError struct {
    Kind      ClaudeErrorKind
    Message   string  // user-safe message extracted from envelope or stderr
    APIStatus int     // 0 if not applicable
    ExitCode  int     // 0 if not applicable
    Cause     error
}

func (e *ClaudeError) Error() string { ... }
func (e *ClaudeError) Unwrap() error { return e.Cause }
```

`ClaudeError` is exported so `cli/explain.go` can `errors.As` it. We
deliberately do NOT define a shared "agent error" abstraction — only Claude
needs this today, and we shouldn't speculatively design a cross-agent
hierarchy. If/when Gemini/OpenCode summarization hits the same problem, we'll
extract.

**Rewire `GenerateText`** in `generate.go`:

After `cmd.Run()`, regardless of whether it returned an error:

1. If `cmd.Run()` returned an `*exec.Error` → `&ClaudeError{Kind: CLIMissing, Cause: err}`. Done.
2. Otherwise, attempt to parse stdout via `parseGenerateTextResponse`.
3. If parsing succeeds and `envelope.IsError` is **false** → return `result`. Done.
4. If parsing succeeds and `envelope.IsError` is **true** → classify into a
   `ClaudeError` using `classifyEnvelopeError(envelope)`:
   - `APIStatus == 401 || APIStatus == 403` → `Auth`
   - `APIStatus == 429` → `RateLimit`
   - `APIStatus >= 400 && APIStatus < 500` → `Config` (e.g., 400 invalid model, 404 model not found)
   - everything else (`APIStatus == 0`, 5xx, etc.) → `Unknown`
   - `Message` = envelope's `Result` field (already user-safe text from Claude)
5. If parsing fails AND `cmd.Run()` returned non-zero exit → fall back to
   `classifyStderrError(stderr, exitCode)`:
   - stderr contains "Invalid API key" or "not logged in" (case-insensitive) → `Auth`
   - else → `Unknown` with `Message: stderr` (truncated to ~500 chars)
6. Context errors (`DeadlineExceeded`, `Canceled`) keep their existing
   sentinel-passthrough behavior.

The stderr substring list for `Auth` is intentionally short (1–2 phrases). It
exists for the case where the CLI crashes before producing an envelope —
treated as best-effort, not authoritative.

### Layer 2 — `summarize/claude.go` and `summarize/summarize.go`

**Two minimal changes:**

1. Drop the `failed to generate summary: %w` wrap inside
   `summarize.GenerateFromTranscript` (it duplicates the wrap in
   `explain.go::generateCheckpointSummary`). Keep the inner errors raw so
   `errors.As(&claudeErr)` still works at the top.
2. In `ClaudeGenerator.Generate`, when the JSON unmarshal of the *summary*
   payload fails, leave the existing "failed to parse summary JSON" wrap as-is
   — that one is genuinely a parse failure (e.g., model returned non-JSON
   prose) and is distinct from `ClaudeError`.

We do NOT add Claude-specific types or debug-flag plumbing here. The
`summarize` package stays agent-agnostic; the typed error flows through via
`%w` and gets unwrapped at the explain layer.

### Layer 1 — `cli/explain.go`

**Add `formatCheckpointSummaryError`:**

```go
func formatCheckpointSummaryError(err error, timeout time.Duration) error {
    var claudeErr *claudecode.ClaudeError
    switch {
    case errors.As(err, &claudeErr):
        switch claudeErr.Kind {
        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorAuth:
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude authentication failed: %s. Run `claude login` and retry", claudeErr.Message)
        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorRateLimit:
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request due to rate limits or quota: %s. Wait and retry", claudeErr.Message)
        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorConfig:
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request: %s. Check your Claude CLI config and selected model", claudeErr.Message)
        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorCLIMissing:
            return errors.New("Claude CLI is not installed or not on PATH")
        default:
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude failed to generate the summary: %s", claudeErr.Message)
        }
    case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
        return fmt.Errorf("Claude did not return a summary within %s. Try again, or set summary_timeout_seconds in .entire/settings.local.json if your transcripts are large", formatSummaryTimeout(timeout))
    case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
        return errors.New("summary generation canceled")
    default:
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate summary: %w", err)
    }
}
```

`generateCheckpointSummary` calls this once on the error returned by
`generateCheckpointAISummary`, and uses the returned error directly (no extra
wrap, fixing the double-prefix issue).

**Add a delayed "Still waiting…" message** as a small helper in `explain.go`:

```go
// startWaitingNotice prints "Still waiting for Claude summary response..."
// once after `delay`, unless the returned cancel function fires first.
func startWaitingNotice(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, delay time.Duration) (cancel func()) {
    if errW == nil { return func() {} }
    timer := time.NewTimer(delay)
    done := make(chan struct{})
    go func() {
        select {
        case <-timer.C:
            fmt.Fprintln(errW, "Still waiting for Claude summary response...")
        case <-done:
            timer.Stop()
        }
    }()
    return func() { close(done) }
}
```

`generateCheckpointSummary` calls it with `delay = 10 * time.Second` before
invoking `generateCheckpointAISummary`, and `defer cancel()`s it.

**Bump the default timeout to 60s and make it overridable** via settings:

- `defaultCheckpointSummaryTimeout = 60 * time.Second` (was 30s).
- Read `summary_timeout_seconds` from `settings.EntireSettings`. If set and
  `>= 1`, use it; otherwise default. Honor it inside
  `generateCheckpointAISummary` so existing parent-deadline logic still applies.

Rationale: the default model is `sonnet` (`summarize/claude.go:51`). A real
summarization on a multi-KB transcript routinely brushes 20–30s even when
nothing is wrong. 30s punishes slow-network and large-transcript users; 60s
still bounds the worst-case hang to a reasonable wait.

### Settings

Add to `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`:

```go
type EntireSettings struct {
    // ...existing fields...
    SummaryTimeoutSeconds int `json:"summary_timeout_seconds,omitempty"`
}
```

Helper:

```go
func SummaryTimeout() time.Duration {
    s, err := Load()
    if err != nil || s.SummaryTimeoutSeconds < 1 {
        return 0 // caller picks default
    }
    return time.Duration(s.SummaryTimeoutSeconds) * time.Second
}
```

`generateCheckpointAISummary` resolves
`timeout := settings.SummaryTimeout(); if timeout == 0 { timeout = checkpointSummaryTimeout }`.

## What we are explicitly NOT doing

These were in the Codex plan; we're dropping them with reasons:

- **`--debug api --debug-file <tempfile>` for connection-error classification.**
  Adds a temp-file lifecycle, a privacy-sensitive log read (CLAUDE.md is
  explicit about not logging user content; debug logs may include prompt
  text), pattern matching against an internal Claude CLI debug format that
  changes between releases, and a permanent extra subprocess flag — all for
  one error category we have no field reports for. If users actually report
  ambiguous timeouts in practice, we'll add this later; for now it fails
  YAGNI.
- **A `connection` error kind.** Without the debug file we cannot reliably
  distinguish "Claude tried Anthropic and got `ECONNREFUSED`" from "Claude is
  just slow." If a real connection error surfaces as `api_error_status: 5xx`
  in the envelope, it falls into `Unknown` with the actual message — which is
  honest. We can split this out later if/when we see the patterns.
- **A shared cross-agent error abstraction.** Only Claude needs typed errors
  today. Premature.

## Tests

`agent/claudecode/response_test.go` (extend):

- Parse envelope with `is_error: true, api_error_status: 401` → `ClaudeError{Kind: Auth}`.
- Parse envelope with `api_error_status: 429` → `RateLimit`.
- Parse envelope with `api_error_status: 404` (invalid model) → `Config`.
- Parse envelope with `is_error: true, api_error_status: nil` → `Unknown` with envelope's `result` as message.
- Success envelope (`is_error: false`) → returns `result`, no error.

`agent/claudecode/claude_test.go` (extend):

- `GenerateText` with stub command runner returning `is_error: true` envelope on stdout, exit 0 → returns `*ClaudeError` with the correct kind.
- `GenerateText` with stub command runner returning non-zero exit + stderr "Invalid API key" → returns `*ClaudeError{Kind: Auth}`.
- `GenerateText` with `*exec.Error` → returns `*ClaudeError{Kind: CLIMissing}`.

`cli/explain_test.go` (extend):

- `formatCheckpointSummaryError` for each `ClaudeErrorKind` produces the expected user-facing string.
- `formatCheckpointSummaryError(context.DeadlineExceeded, 60s)` mentions "60s" and the override hint.
- `formatCheckpointSummaryError(context.Canceled, _)` returns "canceled".
- `startWaitingNotice` prints once after the delay and is silenced by `cancel()`.
- Existing `TestGenerateCheckpointAISummary_*` tests stay green; one new test verifies the 60s default timeout.

## Files touched

- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/response.go` — extend envelope, return parsed struct
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/error.go` — **new** — `ClaudeError` type + classifiers
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/generate.go` — call classifier, return `*ClaudeError`
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/response_test.go` — envelope-parsing tests
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude_test.go` — `GenerateText` failure-path tests
- `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go` — drop one wrap to fix double-prefix
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go` — `formatCheckpointSummaryError`, `startWaitingNotice`, settings-resolved timeout, bump default to 60s
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain_test.go` — formatter and notice tests, updated default-timeout test
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` — add `SummaryTimeoutSeconds` field + helper

## Out of scope (intentional follow-ups)

- Connection-class detection via `--debug-file`. Add only if user reports show a real need.
- Streaming progress messages every 10s up to the timeout (current design fires once at 10s).
- Settings-level validation/clamping for `summary_timeout_seconds` (we just check `>= 1`).
- Surfacing `subtype: error_max_turns` distinctly. The default summarization runs `--print` once with no agentic loop, so this case is unlikely; if observed, route by `subtype` inside `classifyEnvelopeError`.

## Expected outcome

- Auth, rate-limit, and config failures stop being misreported as JSON parse
  errors and instead say what's wrong and how to fix it.
- The generic timeout becomes the fallback for genuinely unclassified hangs,
  with a 60s default that fits real sonnet runs and a settings override for
  outliers.
- A delayed "Still waiting…" message gives users feedback during the wait
  window instead of silent uncertainty.
- Error output is no longer double-prefixed.
- The Claude-specific bits stay in `agent/claudecode/`; `summarize/` stays
  agent-agnostic.

```go
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude authentication failed: %s. Run `claude login` and retry", claudeErr.Message)
        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorRateLimit:
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request due to rate limits or quota: %s. Wait and retry", claudeErr.Message)
        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorConfig:
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request: %s. Check your Claude CLI config and selected model", claudeErr.Message)
        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorCLIMissing:
            return errors.New("Claude CLI is not installed or not on PATH")
        default:
            return fmt.Errorf("Claude failed to generate the summary: %s", claudeErr.Message)
        }
    case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
        return fmt.Errorf("Claude did not return a summary within %s. Try again, or set summary_timeout_seconds in .entire/settings.local.json if your transcripts are large", formatSummaryTimeout(timeout))
    case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
        return errors.New("summary generation canceled")
    default:
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate summary: %w", err)
    }
}
```

`generateCheckpointSummary` calls this once on the error returned by
`generateCheckpointAISummary`, and uses the returned error directly (no extra
wrap, fixing the double-prefix issue).

**Add a delayed "Still waiting…" message** as a small helper in `explain.go`:

```go
// startWaitingNotice prints "Still waiting for Claude summary response..."
// once after `delay`, unless the returned cancel function fires first.
func startWaitingNotice(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, delay time.Duration) (cancel func()) {
    if errW == nil { return func() {} }
    timer := time.NewTimer(delay)
    done := make(chan struct{})
    go func() {
        select {
        case <-timer.C:
            fmt.Fprintln(errW, "Still waiting for Claude summary response...")
        case <-done:
            timer.Stop()
        }
    }()
    return func() { close(done) }
}
```

`generateCheckpointSummary` calls it with `delay = 10 * time.Second` before
invoking `generateCheckpointAISummary`, and `defer cancel()`s it.

**Bump the default timeout to 60s and make it overridable** via settings:

- `defaultCheckpointSummaryTimeout = 60 * time.Second` (was 30s).
- Read `summary_timeout_seconds` from `settings.EntireSettings`. If set and
  `>= 1`, use it; otherwise default. Honor it inside
  `generateCheckpointAISummary` so existing parent-deadline logic still applies.

Rationale: the default model is `sonnet` (`summarize/claude.go:51`). A real
summarization on a multi-KB transcript routinely brushes 20–30s even when
nothing is wrong. 30s punishes slow-network and large-transcript users; 60s
still bounds the worst-case hang to a reasonable wait.

### Settings

Add to `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`:

```go
type EntireSettings struct {
    // ...existing fields...
    SummaryTimeoutSeconds int `json:"summary_timeout_seconds,omitempty"`
}
```

Helper:

```go
func SummaryTimeout() time.Duration {
    s, err := Load()
    if err != nil || s.SummaryTimeoutSeconds < 1 {
        return 0 // caller picks default
    }
    return time.Duration(s.SummaryTimeoutSeconds) * time.Second
}
```

You're right and that's a sharp critique. Let me address it honestly, then revise the doc.

## Honest answer: my current design only partially helps the most common case

If the dominant error users actually see is the timeout, then the typed-error work (auth / rate_limit / config) helps a **minority of cases** — important for the few users who hit them, but not the bulk pain. Three of my proposed changes do help the timeout case directly:

| Change | How it helps the timeout case |
|---|---|
| Bump default 30s → 60s | Most timeouts likely come from sonnet being legitimately slow on a multi-KB transcript, not from Claude actually hanging. Doubling the window cuts false-positive timeouts. |
| `summary_timeout_seconds` in settings | Users with large transcripts or slow networks can opt up to 120s/180s without code changes. |
| Delayed "Still waiting…" message | Doesn't fix the failure but kills the silent-wait perception. |

That's it. Everything else I designed is for the minority cases. **The current design does not actually distinguish "Claude is hung" from "Claude is slow,"** which is the diagnostic question the user actually wants answered when a timeout fires.

## What would actually distinguish hung vs slow

The honest answer is **stream-mode**, not the debug-file Codex proposed. Claude CLI supports `--output-format stream-json`, which emits incremental events as the model produces output. If we consume that stream we can:

- Track "time since last byte from Claude"
- Treat the timeout as **idle-based, not wall-clock**: 60s of *no progress at all* → genuinely hung; bytes still flowing → keep waiting
- Tell the user *which* it was when we abort

This is a real architectural change (different output format, parser rewrite, idle-tracking timer) — bigger than the current design's scope. But it's the right tool for the diagnostic question. The debug-file approach in Codex's plan was trying to reach the same answer through a much messier door.

## What I'm changing in the design

Two updates:

1. **Make the timeout error message itself diagnostic.** Even without stream-mode, list the three concrete causes and what to try, so the user has a remediation path the moment they see it. This is the cheapest and biggest UX win for the most-common case.
2. **Promote stream-mode from "out of scope" to "explicit follow-up with rationale."** So you can decide whether to bundle it in this PR or do it next.

--include-partial-messages`, which emits incremental events as the model
produces output. With stream-mode wired in we could:

- Replace the wall-clock timeout with an **idle-based timeout**: 60s of *no
  progress at all* means genuinely hung; bytes still flowing means slow but
  alive.
- Tell the user *which* it was when we abort:

    longer timeout."
  - "Claude has been idle for 60s — likely hung. Try `claude --print 'hi'`
    from a shell."

Yes — that's a much better UX direction. The size info is right there in the call site (we have `scopedTranscript` as bytes before we hand it off), so we can both pick a proportional timeout *and* tell the user what we're doing, with no manual config required for the common case. Let me revise.

## What I'd change

- **Adaptive timeout** based on transcript size, computed in `generateCheckpointAISummary`. Continuous formula, capped on both ends. No size buckets — those are arbitrary and create cliffs at the boundaries.
- **Pre-flight message** that surfaces the size and expected wait window, so the user understands why the wait is what it is.
- **Settings override demoted to escape hatch.** It still exists for "my network is reliably slow, force 300s on everything" or "I want to fail fast" cases, but it's no longer the user's first lever.
- **Timeout error message** updated so it doesn't hardcode "60s" and tells the user what timeout actually applied to their run.

Honest caveat I'll write into the doc: the proportional formula's constants (seconds per KB) are an educated guess. We don't have empirical data on Claude's input-size-to-wall-clock curve. I'll pick conservative starting values and explicitly call them out as tunable, so a future PR can adjust them with real telemetry.

content.text:
That's a much better framing of the actual problem. Let me think out loud, because you're calling out something I missed.

## What the user actually complained about originally

Re-reading PR 876's description: `^Cfailed to generate summary: failed to generate summary: claude CLI failed (exit -1):`. The user pressed Ctrl+C because they had no idea what was happening. The complaint was **silence**, not duration. PR 876 read that as "we need to bound the wait" but the real fix was "we need to make the wait observable."

If we make the wait observable, then **the user becomes the timeout.** They see "still working… 1m elapsed", and they decide whether to Ctrl+C. That's strictly more informed than us guessing 30s or 60s or 300s for them.

## When we still need a hard timeout

There's exactly one case: **non-interactive invocation** (CI, scripts, background auto-summarize). No human is watching, no Ctrl+C is coming, the process needs to bound itself or it'll hang the parent indefinitely.

So the cleaner design is:

- **TTY (interactive):** no deadline. Rich progress: pre-flight size message at t=0, periodic "still working… Ns elapsed" updates, with a clear "Press Ctrl+C to cancel" hint after the first minute. The user is the timeout.
- **Non-TTY (CI / background):** generous safety deadline (default 5 minutes, not 30s — it's a hang-guard, not a UX guess). Settings override available.
- **Settings override** can also force a deadline in interactive mode if a user *wants* the hard cap (e.g., known-flaky env, wants fast failure).

The typed-error work (auth / rate_limit / config / cli_missing) still applies — those are independent of the timeout question, they're about classifying *real* failures when Claude returns one. Nothing about that changes.

## The honest tradeoff

You give up the property "the user is guaranteed to get an error within N seconds" in interactive mode. In exchange you get:
- No more aborting useful work because we picked a timeout that was too short
- The wait is observable so the user has agency
- The interactive UX matches the actual mental model: "I asked Claude to do something, it's working, I'll wait or cancel"

Two things to verify before I commit to this direction in the design:

1. **Does Ctrl+C reliably kill the Claude subprocess?** The current code uses `exec.CommandContext` which sends SIGKILL on context cancellation, and the existing context-cancel handling in `generate.go:43-48` already returns `context.Canceled`. So yes — Ctrl+C → ctx canceled → cmd killed → clean error path. Already works.

2. **Is there an `auto-summarize` path that runs after sessions and currently relies on this same code?** I should check before I commit to "TTY-gated timeout" — if auto-summarize calls `generateCheckpointAISummary`, removing the timeout there would be wrong.

Want me to verify #2 quickly, then update the design with this direction? Or do you want to push further on the framing first?

1	# Design: Actionable error classification for `entire explain --generate`
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-04-15
4	**Status:** Draft, awaiting review
5	**Related PR:** #876 (added the 30s timeout this design is refining)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	PR #876 added a 30-second timeout around checkpoint summary generation so that
10	`entire explain --generate` can no longer hang indefinitely when the Claude CLI
11	stalls. That fix replaced a "hangs forever, user has to Ctrl+C" failure with a
12	"hangs for 30 seconds, then prints `summary generation timed out after 30s`"
13	failure.
14	
15	Two follow-up problems remain:
16	
17	1. **Real Claude CLI failures are misclassified as parse failures or as
18	   ambiguous timeouts.** The Claude CLI returns most operational failures
19	   (auth, rate limit, invalid model, malformed request) as **exit 0** with a
20	   structured `is_error: true` envelope on stdout. The current code discards
21	   `is_error` and tries to JSON-parse the error string as a `Summary`, so the
22	   user sees `failed to parse summary JSON: ... (response: <error text>)`. That
23	   message is unactionable.
24	2. **The 30s timeout message is generic.** When it fires, the user has no way
25	   to tell whether Claude was actually hung, was slow on a long transcript, or
26	   had a network problem.
27	
28	A third, smaller issue worth fixing in the same change:
29	
30	3. **Errors get double-wrapped.** Today's output reads
31	   `failed to generate summary: failed to generate summary: claude CLI failed (exit -1):`
32	   because both `summarize.GenerateFromTranscript` and
33	   `cli/explain.go::generateCheckpointSummary` wrap with the same prefix.
34	
35	### Where the user pain actually concentrates
36	
37	Field experience strongly suggests the **most-seen failure is the timeout itself**,
38	not auth or rate-limit. Typed errors for auth/rate-limit/config matter for the
39	minority of users who hit them, but they do not address the dominant case. This
40	design must therefore be honest about what it does and does not fix for the
41	most common case:
42	
43	| What this design does for "30s timed out" | |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| Bumps default to 60s + settings override | Cuts false-positive timeouts where sonnet was just slow |
46	| Replaces the generic timeout string with a diagnostic message | Gives the user concrete causes and remediation steps the moment they see it |
47	| Adds delayed "Still waiting…" notice at 10s | Removes silent-wait uncertainty (does not change the outcome) |
48	| Does **not** distinguish "Claude hung" vs "Claude slow" | See "Stream-mode follow-up" below |
49	
50	## Current code path
51	
52	Three layers, top to bottom:
53	
54	1. `cli/explain.go::generateCheckpointAISummary` — wraps the call in a 30s
55	   `context.WithTimeout`, translates `DeadlineExceeded` and `Canceled` into
56	   user-facing strings.
57	2. `summarize/claude.go::ClaudeGenerator.Generate` — agent-agnostic; calls
58	   `agent.TextGenerator.GenerateText(...)` and JSON-parses the result string
59	   into a `checkpoint.Summary`.
60	3. `agent/claudecode/generate.go::ClaudeCodeAgent.GenerateText` — runs
61	   `claude --print --output-format json --model X --setting-sources ""`,
62	   observes stdout/stderr/exit codes, dispatches the response through
63	   `agent/claudecode/response.go::parseGenerateTextResponse`.
64	
65	The seam where stdout, stderr, and exit code are all visible is layer 3 —
66	`agent/claudecode`. Anything that needs to read the Claude error envelope or
67	classify by `api_error_status` belongs there.
68	
69	## Findings from probing the live `claude` CLI
70	
71	These results drive the design:
72	
73	| Failure                                  | Exit | stdout JSON                                                         |
74	| ---------------------------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
75	| Success                                  | 0    | `{"is_error":false, "subtype":"success", "result":"..."}`           |
76	| Invalid model (`--model nonexistent`)    | 0    | `{"is_error":true, "api_error_status":404, "result":"There's an issue with the selected model..."}` |
77	| Empty model (`--model ""`)               | 0    | `{"is_error":true, "api_error_status":400, "result":"API Error: 400 ... invalid_request_error ..."}` |
78	| Binary missing                           | 127  | (no envelope; produces `exec.Error` in Go)                          |
79	
80	The two most useful insights:
81	
82	- **Operational errors return exit 0**, not non-zero. Any classification gated
83	  on "non-zero exit" misses every probed failure mode. The envelope must be
84	  parsed and `is_error` checked **on every successful subprocess run**.
85	- **`subtype` and `api_error_status` are usable** for classification today.
86	
87	## Design
88	
89	### Layer 3 — `agent/claudecode/`
90	
91	**Extend the response envelope** in `response.go`:
92	
93	```go
94	type responseEnvelope struct {
95	    Type           string  `json:"type"`
96	    Subtype        string  `json:"subtype"`
97	    IsError        bool    `json:"is_error"`
98	    APIErrorStatus *int    `json:"api_error_status"`
99	    Result         *string `json:"result"`
100	}
101	```
102	
103	`parseGenerateTextResponse` keeps its current "single object or array of
104	events" behavior, but also returns the parsed envelope (not just the result
105	string), so callers can branch on `IsError`.
106	
107	**Add a typed error** in a new file `agent/claudecode/error.go`:
108	
109	```go
110	type ClaudeErrorKind string
111	
112	const (
113	    ClaudeErrorAuth       ClaudeErrorKind = "auth"
114	    ClaudeErrorConfig     ClaudeErrorKind = "config"
115	    ClaudeErrorRateLimit  ClaudeErrorKind = "rate_limit"
116	    ClaudeErrorCLIMissing ClaudeErrorKind = "cli_missing"
117	    ClaudeErrorUnknown    ClaudeErrorKind = "unknown"
118	)
119	
120	type ClaudeError struct {
121	    Kind      ClaudeErrorKind
122	    Message   string  // user-safe message extracted from envelope or stderr
123	    APIStatus int     // 0 if not applicable
124	    ExitCode  int     // 0 if not applicable
125	    Cause     error
126	}
127	
128	func (e *ClaudeError) Error() string { ... }
129	func (e *ClaudeError) Unwrap() error { return e.Cause }
130	```
131	
132	`ClaudeError` is exported so `cli/explain.go` can `errors.As` it. We
133	deliberately do NOT define a shared "agent error" abstraction — only Claude
134	needs this today, and we shouldn't speculatively design a cross-agent
135	hierarchy. If/when Gemini/OpenCode summarization hits the same problem, we'll
136	extract.
137	
138	**Rewire `GenerateText`** in `generate.go`:
139	
140	After `cmd.Run()`, regardless of whether it returned an error:
141	
142	1. If `cmd.Run()` returned an `*exec.Error` → `&ClaudeError{Kind: CLIMissing, Cause: err}`. Done.
143	2. Otherwise, attempt to parse stdout via `parseGenerateTextResponse`.
144	3. If parsing succeeds and `envelope.IsError` is **false** → return `result`. Done.
145	4. If parsing succeeds and `envelope.IsError` is **true** → classify into a
146	   `ClaudeError` using `classifyEnvelopeError(envelope)`:
147	   - `APIStatus == 401 || APIStatus == 403` → `Auth`
148	   - `APIStatus == 429` → `RateLimit`
149	   - `APIStatus >= 400 && APIStatus < 500` → `Config` (e.g., 400 invalid model, 404 model not found)
150	   - everything else (`APIStatus == 0`, 5xx, etc.) → `Unknown`
151	   - `Message` = envelope's `Result` field (already user-safe text from Claude)
152	5. If parsing fails AND `cmd.Run()` returned non-zero exit → fall back to
153	   `classifyStderrError(stderr, exitCode)`:
154	   - stderr contains "Invalid API key" or "not logged in" (case-insensitive) → `Auth`
155	   - else → `Unknown` with `Message: stderr` (truncated to ~500 chars)
156	6. Context errors (`DeadlineExceeded`, `Canceled`) keep their existing
157	   sentinel-passthrough behavior.
158	
159	The stderr substring list for `Auth` is intentionally short (1–2 phrases). It
160	exists for the case where the CLI crashes before producing an envelope —
161	treated as best-effort, not authoritative.
162	
163	### Layer 2 — `summarize/claude.go` and `summarize/summarize.go`
164	
165	**Two minimal changes:**
166	
167	1. Drop the `failed to generate summary: %w` wrap inside
168	   `summarize.GenerateFromTranscript` (it duplicates the wrap in
169	   `explain.go::generateCheckpointSummary`). Keep the inner errors raw so
170	   `errors.As(&claudeErr)` still works at the top.
171	2. In `ClaudeGenerator.Generate`, when the JSON unmarshal of the *summary*
172	   payload fails, leave the existing "failed to parse summary JSON" wrap as-is
173	   — that one is genuinely a parse failure (e.g., model returned non-JSON
174	   prose) and is distinct from `ClaudeError`.
175	
176	We do NOT add Claude-specific types or debug-flag plumbing here. The
177	`summarize` package stays agent-agnostic; the typed error flows through via
178	`%w` and gets unwrapped at the explain layer.
179	
180	### Layer 1 — `cli/explain.go`
181	
182	**Add `formatCheckpointSummaryError`:**
183	
184	```go
185	func formatCheckpointSummaryError(err error, timeout time.Duration) error {
186	    var claudeErr *claudecode.ClaudeError
187	    switch {
188	    case errors.As(err, &claudeErr):
189	        switch claudeErr.Kind {
190	        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorAuth:
191	            return fmt.Errorf("Claude authentication failed: %s. Run `claude login` and retry", claudeErr.Message)
192	        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorRateLimit:
193	            return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request due to rate limits or quota: %s. Wait and retry", claudeErr.Message)
194	        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorConfig:
195	            return fmt.Errorf("Claude rejected the summary request: %s. Check your Claude CLI config and selected model", claudeErr.Message)
196	        case claudecode.ClaudeErrorCLIMissing:
197	            return errors.New("Claude CLI is not installed or not on PATH")
198	        default:
199	            return fmt.Errorf("Claude failed to generate the summary: %s", claudeErr.Message)
200	        }
201	    case errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
202	        return fmt.Errorf(
203	            "Claude did not return a summary within %s. This usually means one of:\n"+
204	                "  - sonnet is taking longer than expected on a large transcript\n"+
205	                "    Try: set `summary_timeout_seconds: 120` in .entire/settings.local.json\n"+
206	                "  - the Claude CLI cannot reach Anthropic's API (network, VPN, firewall)\n"+
207	                "    Try: run `claude --print \"hi\"` from a shell to confirm the CLI works\n"+
208	                "  - Anthropic's API is degraded\n"+
209	                "    Check: https://status.anthropic.com",
210	            formatSummaryTimeout(timeout))
211	    case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
212	        return errors.New("summary generation canceled")
213	    default:
214	        return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate summary: %w", err)
215	    }
216	}
217	```
218	
219	`generateCheckpointSummary` calls this once on the error returned by
220	`generateCheckpointAISummary`, and uses the returned error directly (no extra
221	wrap, fixing the double-prefix issue).
222	
223	**Add a delayed "Still waiting…" message** as a small helper in `explain.go`:
224	
225	```go
226	// startWaitingNotice prints "Still waiting for Claude summary response..."
227	// once after `delay`, unless the returned cancel function fires first.
228	func startWaitingNotice(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, delay time.Duration) (cancel func()) {
229	    if errW == nil { return func() {} }
230	    timer := time.NewTimer(delay)
231	    done := make(chan struct{})
232	    go func() {
233	        select {
234	        case <-timer.C:
235	            fmt.Fprintln(errW, "Still waiting for Claude summary response...")
236	        case <-done:
237	            timer.Stop()
238	        }
239	    }()
240	    return func() { close(done) }
241	}
242	```
243	
244	`generateCheckpointSummary` calls it with `delay = 10 * time.Second` before
245	invoking `generateCheckpointAISummary`, and `defer cancel()`s it.
246	
247	**Bump the default timeout to 60s and make it overridable** via settings:
248	
249	- `defaultCheckpointSummaryTimeout = 60 * time.Second` (was 30s).
250	- Read `summary_timeout_seconds` from `settings.EntireSettings`. If set and
251	  `>= 1`, use it; otherwise default. Honor it inside
252	  `generateCheckpointAISummary` so existing parent-deadline logic still applies.
253	
254	Rationale: the default model is `sonnet` (`summarize/claude.go:51`). A real
255	summarization on a multi-KB transcript routinely brushes 20–30s even when
256	nothing is wrong. 30s punishes slow-network and large-transcript users; 60s
257	still bounds the worst-case hang to a reasonable wait.
258	
259	### Settings
260	
261	Add to `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`:
262	
263	```go
264	type EntireSettings struct {
265	    // ...existing fields...
266	    SummaryTimeoutSeconds int `json:"summary_timeout_seconds,omitempty"`
267	}
268	```
269	
270	Helper:
271	
272	```go
273	func SummaryTimeout() time.Duration {
274	    s, err := Load()
275	    if err != nil || s.SummaryTimeoutSeconds < 1 {
276	        return 0 // caller picks default
277	    }
278	    return time.Duration(s.SummaryTimeoutSeconds) * time.Second
279	}
280	```
281	
282	`generateCheckpointAISummary` resolves
283	`timeout := settings.SummaryTimeout(); if timeout == 0 { timeout = checkpointSummaryTimeout }`.
284	
285	## What we are explicitly NOT doing
286	
287	These were in the Codex plan; we're dropping them with reasons:
288	
289	- **`--debug api --debug-file <tempfile>` for connection-error classification.**
290	  Adds a temp-file lifecycle, a privacy-sensitive log read (CLAUDE.md is
291	  explicit about not logging user content; debug logs may include prompt
292	  text), pattern matching against an internal Claude CLI debug format that
293	  changes between releases, and a permanent extra subprocess flag — all for
294	  one error category we have no field reports for. If users actually report
295	  ambiguous timeouts in practice, we'll add this later; for now it fails
296	  YAGNI.
297	- **A `connection` error kind.** Without the debug file we cannot reliably
298	  distinguish "Claude tried Anthropic and got `ECONNREFUSED`" from "Claude is
299	  just slow." If a real connection error surfaces as `api_error_status: 5xx`
300	  in the envelope, it falls into `Unknown` with the actual message — which is
301	  honest. We can split this out later if/when we see the patterns.
302	- **A shared cross-agent error abstraction.** Only Claude needs typed errors
303	  today. Premature.
304	
305	## Tests
306	
307	`agent/claudecode/response_test.go` (extend):
308	
309	- Parse envelope with `is_error: true, api_error_status: 401` → `ClaudeError{Kind: Auth}`.
310	- Parse envelope with `api_error_status: 429` → `RateLimit`.
311	- Parse envelope with `api_error_status: 404` (invalid model) → `Config`.
312	- Parse envelope with `is_error: true, api_error_status: nil` → `Unknown` with envelope's `result` as message.
313	- Success envelope (`is_error: false`) → returns `result`, no error.
314	
315	`agent/claudecode/claude_test.go` (extend):
316	
317	- `GenerateText` with stub command runner returning `is_error: true` envelope on stdout, exit 0 → returns `*ClaudeError` with the correct kind.
318	- `GenerateText` with stub command runner returning non-zero exit + stderr "Invalid API key" → returns `*ClaudeError{Kind: Auth}`.
319	- `GenerateText` with `*exec.Error` → returns `*ClaudeError{Kind: CLIMissing}`.
320	
321	`cli/explain_test.go` (extend):
322	
323	- `formatCheckpointSummaryError` for each `ClaudeErrorKind` produces the expected user-facing string.
324	- `formatCheckpointSummaryError(context.DeadlineExceeded, 60s)` mentions "60s" and the override hint.
325	- `formatCheckpointSummaryError(context.Canceled, _)` returns "canceled".
326	- `startWaitingNotice` prints once after the delay and is silenced by `cancel()`.
327	- Existing `TestGenerateCheckpointAISummary_*` tests stay green; one new test verifies the 60s default timeout.
328	
329	## Files touched
330	
331	- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/response.go` — extend envelope, return parsed struct
332	- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/error.go` — **new** — `ClaudeError` type + classifiers
333	- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/generate.go` — call classifier, return `*ClaudeError`
334	- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/response_test.go` — envelope-parsing tests
335	- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude_test.go` — `GenerateText` failure-path tests
336	- `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go` — drop one wrap to fix double-prefix
337	- `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go` — `formatCheckpointSummaryError`, `startWaitingNotice`, settings-resolved timeout, bump default to 60s
338	- `cmd/entire/cli/explain_test.go` — formatter and notice tests, updated default-timeout test
339	- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` — add `SummaryTimeoutSeconds` field + helper
340	
341	## Stream-mode follow-up (the real fix for the most common case)
342	
343	This design intentionally **does not** add the ability to distinguish "Claude
344	hung" from "Claude is just slow." That diagnostic is what the user actually
345	wants when a timeout fires, and the right tool for it is **stream-mode**, not
346	the debug-file approach Codex proposed.
347	
348	`claude --print` supports `--output-format stream-json
349	--include-partial-messages`, which emits incremental events as the model
350	produces output. With stream-mode wired in we could:
351	
352	- Track "time since last byte received from Claude."
353	- Replace the wall-clock timeout with an **idle-based timeout**: 60s of *no
354	  progress at all* means genuinely hung; bytes still flowing means slow but
355	  alive.
356	- Tell the user *which* it was when we abort:
357	  - "Claude was still producing output but did not finish within 60s — try a
358	    longer timeout."
359	  - "Claude has been idle for 60s — likely hung. Try `claude --print 'hi'`
360	    from a shell."
361	
362	This is a real architectural change (different output format, parser rewrite
363	in `agent/claudecode/response.go` to consume the event stream, idle-tracking
364	timer in `GenerateText`, new test surface) and is intentionally **out of
365	scope** for this design. It belongs in a follow-up because:
366	
367	- The current design is shippable on its own and delivers the cheap, high-leverage wins (typed errors, 60s default, settings override, diagnostic timeout message, delayed notice, fixed double-wrap).
368	- Stream-mode is a focused, well-bounded next change with its own design surface.
369	- Doing both at once doubles the risk in the parser/classifier code and obscures which change resolved which class of report.
370	
371	If field reports after this change still show timeout dominance, stream-mode
372	is the next investment — not debug-file parsing.
373	
374	## Other intentional non-goals
375	
376	- **Connection-class detection via `--debug-file`.** Privacy-sensitive log
377	  read, brittle pattern matching against an internal Claude CLI debug format,
378	  permanent extra subprocess flag — all for one error category that
379	  stream-mode would solve more cleanly.
380	- **A `connection` error kind.** Without diagnostic data we can't reliably
381	  distinguish "Claude tried Anthropic and got `ECONNREFUSED`" from "Claude is
382	  just slow." If a real connection error surfaces as `api_error_status: 5xx`
383	  in the envelope, it falls into `Unknown` with the actual message — which is
384	  honest. Revisit alongside stream-mode.
385	- **A shared cross-agent error abstraction.** Only Claude needs typed errors today. Premature.
386	- **Streaming "Still waiting…" every 10s up to the timeout.** Current design fires once at 10s.
387	- **Settings-level validation/clamping for `summary_timeout_seconds`.** We just check `>= 1`.
388	- **Surfacing `subtype: error_max_turns` distinctly.** The default summarization runs `--print` once with no agentic loop, so this case is unlikely; if observed, route by `subtype` inside `classifyEnvelopeError`.
389	
390	## Expected outcome
391	
392	For the **dominant case (timeout):**
393	- Default timeout doubles (30s → 60s) — fewer false-positive timeouts on slow
394	  sonnet runs.
395	- The timeout error message itself becomes diagnostic, listing the three
396	  concrete causes and the exact remediation step for each.
397	- `summary_timeout_seconds` setting lets users with consistently large
398	  transcripts opt up without code changes.
399	- Delayed "Still waiting…" notice removes silent-wait uncertainty.
400	
401	For the **minority cases (auth, rate_limit, config):**
402	- Stop being misreported as JSON parse errors and instead say what's wrong
403	  and how to fix it.
404	
405	For everything:
406	- Error output is no longer double-prefixed.
407	- The Claude-specific bits stay in `agent/claudecode/`; `summarize/` stays
408	  agent-agnostic.
409	
410	What this design **does not** fix (deferred to stream-mode follow-up):
411	- Distinguishing "Claude is hung" from "Claude is slow" inside the timeout.
412	  See "Stream-mode follow-up" above.
413
